```
completion(prompt, model?="default"|"smol"|"slow", system?=None, schema?=None) → handle; `.wait()` returns text (parsed with `schema`). Stateless, no tools/history.
await judge(state, questions, images?=[path | ImageContent, …]) → `{id: answer}`
    Typed judgment over one `state` (str | JSON object | JSON array). Every question sees the same state and is answered independently: batch independent questions into one call. Cheap and fast (TypeSafe when credentialed, else the tiny/smol chat model); prefer over `completion()` for classification, yes/no, ranking. Two or more states → `judge_batch`, never a loop of `judge()`.
    `questions`: `{id: q}` where q is one of
      `{type: "choice", instructions, criteria: {label: rubric | None, …}}` → `{choice, probabilities: {label: p}, confidence}` (≥2 labels)
      `{type: "bool", instructions, criteria?: {true?: str, false?: str}}` → `{bool: P(yes)}`
      `{type: "score", instructions, criteria: [lowest, …, highest]}` → `{score, probabilities: {"0": p, …}, confidence}` (≥2 levels; score is the probability-weighted level index)
judge_batch(states, questions, concurrency?=32, retries?=1, min_ok?=1, intent?=None, images?={key: [path | ImageContent, …]}) → JudgmentBatch
    Images accept local paths or embedded `ImageContent`; batch attachments map each state key to its list (array inputs use zero-based index keys). Image requests skip candidates without image support, never silently drop images, and fail if no compatible judge remains.
    Same `questions` over every state (`{key: state}` or a list keyed by index), run and owned by the host — it outlives the cell. `intent` is an optional nonempty progress/job label (default `"Judging"`). Returns at once; pull settled items in bounded slices across cells: `await b.drain(timeout?)` → `[(key, item)]` settled since the last drain (`[]` on timeout; `item.answers` on success, else `item.error`, never raised); `async for k, item in b.drain_iter(timeout)` until timeout or completion; `b.status()` → `{intent, done, total, failed, cost, running, model}`; `b.results()` → `{key: answers}` so far; `b.failed()` → `{key: error}`; `b.cancel()`; `b.close()` releases it. `drain()` raises only when the run died wholesale (no judge, or fewer than `min_ok` answered). `b.id` is an async job id: completion auto-delivers a summary, `wait` blocks when you have nothing else to do, `judge_batch.attach(id)` re-creates the ref after a reset.
```

# The fstab noauto entry is mounted explicitly after S12op-release-activate.

PATH=/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH
fail() { printf 'mount-3tchedfs: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
case "${1:-}" in
    start)
        [ "$#" = 1 ] || exit 2
        mount /run/mounts/3tchedFS
        exec mount /run/mounts/threetched
        ;;
    stop) exit 0 ;;
esac
[ "$(id -u)" = 0 ] || fail 'host mount owner must be root'
[ "$#" = 4 ] && [ "$3" = -o ] ||
    fail 'expected the declared 3tchedFS fstab entry'
fs_name=$1
mount_path=$2
case "$fs_name:$mount_path" in
    3tchedFS:/run/mounts/3tchedFS) selection=--exclude-plugin ;;
    threetched:/run/mounts/threetched) selection=--include-plugin ;;
    *) fail 'unexpected mount source or target' ;;
esac
upstream_plugins=threetched,tched_router,tched_plugins,tched_skills
catalog=/usr/share/op-dbus/plugin-blobs
options=$4
while [ -n "$options" ]; do
    option=${options%%,*}
    case "$option" in
        rw|noauto|nosuid|nodev|noexec|noatime|defaults) ;;
        *) fail "unsupported mount option: $option" ;;
    esac
    case "$options" in *,*) options=${options#*,} ;; *) options= ;; esac
done
protected_file() {
    [ -f "$1" ] && [ ! -L "$1" ] || return 1
    case "$(stat -c '%u:%g:%a' "$1")" in 0:0:400|0:0:600) return 0 ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
}
session_file=/etc/op-dbus/human-lungs-session
owner_file=/etc/op-dbus/human-lungs-call-owner-uid
protected_file "$session_file" && protected_file "$owner_file" || fail 'unsafe or absent host identity selection'
session=$(tr -d '[:space:]' <"$session_file")
printf '%s\n' "$session" | grep -Eq '^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$' || fail 'invalid session'
owner_uid=$(tr -d '[:space:]' <"$owner_file")
case "$owner_uid" in ''|*[!0-9]*) fail 'invalid local caller UID' ;; esac
[ "$owner_uid" = "$(id -u jeremy)" ] || fail 'local operator UID changed'
ensure_dir() {
    if [ ! -e "$1" ] && [ ! -L "$1" ]; then mkdir -m "$2" "$1"; fi

        fail "unsafe directory: $1"
}
ensure_dir /run/opdbus 755
ensure_dir /run/opdbus/host-fuse 700
runtime=/run/opdbus/host-fuse/$fs_name
ensure_dir "$runtime" 700
umask 077
exec 9>"$runtime/adapter.lock"
flock -w 15 9 || fail 'another mount invocation is active'
mounted_kind() { findmnt -rn -M "$mount_path" -o FSTYPE; }
ready() {
    [ "$(mounted_kind)" = fuse.3tchedFS ] || return 1
    [ "$(findmnt -rn -M "$mount_path" -o SOURCE)" = "$fs_name" ] || return 1
    timeout 3 jq -e --arg session "$session" --argjson uid "$owner_uid" '
        .mount_identity.kind == "host_session" and
        .mount_identity.session == $session and
        .local_call_owner_uid == $uid and .workspace_id == null
    ' "$mount_path/.3tchedfs.json" >/dev/null || return 1
    timeout 3 jq -e --arg name "$fs_name" --arg upstream "$upstream_plugins" \
        --slurpfile catalog "$catalog/.manifest.json" '
        ($upstream | split(",") | sort) as $upstream |
        (.objects | keys | sort) as $actual |
        (.source_catalog_hash == $catalog[0].catalog_hash and
         .source_catalog_generation == $catalog[0].generation) and
        (if $name == "threetched" then $actual == $upstream
        else (.objects | has("tched_fs")) and
            ($actual == (($catalog[0].plugins | keys | sort) - $upstream))
        end)
    ' "$mount_path/view.json" >/dev/null

    ready || fail 'existing mount differs from the declared identity or release view'
    date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ >"$runtime/fstab-ready-at"

store=/dev/shm/3tchedfs-$fs_name

    --catalog /dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs --state /dev/shm/opdbus/state \
    --allow-other --auto-unmount --call-owner-uid "$owner_uid" \
    --lungs-socket /run/opdbus/lungs/lungs.sock --lungs-session "$session" \
    "$mount_path" >"$runtime/daemon.log" 2>&1 </dev/null 9>&- &
daemon_pid=$!
printf '%s\n' "$daemon_pid" >"$runtime/daemon.pid"
attempt=0
while [ "$attempt" -lt 100 ]; do
    if ready; then
        date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ >"$runtime/fstab-ready-at"
        exit 0
    fi
    kill -0 "$daemon_pid" 2>/dev/null || break
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    sleep 0.1
done
kill "$daemon_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
wait "$daemon_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
fail "mount did not become ready; see $runtime/daemon.log"

[`threetched-surface.rs:180`](/srv/git/odbus-verified/crates/threetched-fs/src/threetched-surface.rs:180) captures `config schema`, recursive `--help`, and `--version`, then checks that the binary did not change. `schema_from_capture` turns that into the `threetched` PluginSchema, including per-command capabilities.
4. The sealer obtains each registered plugin's schema. [`op-blob/src/lib.rs:72`](/srv/git/odbus-verified/crates/op-blob/src/lib.rs:72) canonicalizes and seals the **full** PluginSchema in `SCHEMA_JSON`; reflection/manifest views derive from that same value.
5. [`catalog.rs:153`](/srv/git/odbus-verified/crates/op-blob/src/catalog.rs:153) writes `<plugin_id>.<schema_hash16>.blob` and updates the catalog. A full reseal removes IDs absent from the build via `retain_plugins`.
6. Golden preparation validates/stages an already sealed catalog. Deployment transports the snapshot; FUSE projects its blobs. FUSE does not invent or reseal an upstream schema when a file is read.

#!/bin/sh
### BEGIN INIT INFO
# Provides:          op-3tchedfs-mount
# Required-Start:    op-release-activate
# Required-Stop:
# Default-Start:     S
# Default-Stop:
# Short-Description: Mount separate OP-DBUS and threetched views from fstab
### END INIT INFO
# The release stages this adapter in /usr/local/libexec/op-dbus/helpers.
# /usr/sbin/mount.fuse.3tchedFS and rcS/S13op-3tchedfs-mount link there.
# The fstab noauto entry is mounted explicitly after S12op-release-activate.
set -eu
PATH=/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH
fail() { printf 'mount-3tchedfs: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
case "${1:-}" in
    start)
        [ "$#" = 1 ] || exit 2
        mount /run/mounts/3tchedFS
        exec mount /run/mounts/threetched
        ;;
    stop) exit 0 ;;
esac
[ "$(id -u)" = 0 ] || fail 'host mount owner must be root'
[ "$#" = 4 ] && [ "$3" = -o ] ||
    fail 'expected the declared 3tchedFS fstab entry'
fs_name=$1
mount_path=$2
case "$fs_name:$mount_path" in
    3tchedFS:/run/mounts/3tchedFS) selection=--exclude-plugin ;;
    threetched:/run/mounts/threetched) selection=--include-plugin ;;
    *) fail 'unexpected mount source or target' ;;
esac
upstream_plugins=threetched,tched_router,tched_plugins,tched_skills
catalog=/usr/share/op-dbus/plugin-blobs
options=$4
while [ -n "$options" ]; do
    option=${options%%,*}
    case "$option" in
        rw|noauto|nosuid|nodev|noexec|noatime|defaults) ;;
        *) fail "unsupported mount option: $option" ;;
    esac
    case "$options" in *,*) options=${options#*,} ;; *) options= ;; esac
done
protected_file() {
    [ -f "$1" ] && [ ! -L "$1" ] || return 1
    case "$(stat -c '%u:%g:%a' "$1")" in 0:0:400|0:0:600) return 0 ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
}
session_file=/etc/op-dbus/human-lungs-session
owner_file=/etc/op-dbus/human-lungs-call-owner-uid
protected_file "$session_file" && protected_file "$owner_file" || fail 'unsafe or absent host identity selection'
session=$(tr -d '[:space:]' <"$session_file")
printf '%s\n' "$session" | grep -Eq '^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$' || fail 'invalid session'
owner_uid=$(tr -d '[:space:]' <"$owner_file")
case "$owner_uid" in ''|*[!0-9]*) fail 'invalid local caller UID' ;; esac
[ "$owner_uid" = "$(id -u jeremy)" ] || fail 'local operator UID changed'
ensure_dir() {
    if [ ! -e "$1" ] && [ ! -L "$1" ]; then mkdir -m "$2" "$1"; fi
    [ -d "$1" ] && [ ! -L "$1" ] && [ "$(stat -c '%u:%g:%a' "$1")" = "0:0:$2" ] ||
        fail "unsafe directory: $1"
}
ensure_dir /run/opdbus 755
ensure_dir /run/opdbus/host-fuse 700
runtime=/run/opdbus/host-fuse/$fs_name
ensure_dir "$runtime" 700
umask 077
exec 9>"$runtime/adapter.lock"
flock -w 15 9 || fail 'another mount invocation is active'
mounted_kind() { findmnt -rn -M "$mount_path" -o FSTYPE; }
ready() {
    [ "$(mounted_kind)" = fuse.3tchedFS ] || return 1
    [ "$(findmnt -rn -M "$mount_path" -o SOURCE)" = "$fs_name" ] || return 1
    timeout 3 jq -e --arg session "$session" --argjson uid "$owner_uid" '
        .mount_identity.kind == "host_session" and
        .mount_identity.session == $session and
        .local_call_owner_uid == $uid and .workspace_id == null
    ' "$mount_path/.3tchedfs.json" >/dev/null || return 1
    timeout 3 jq -e --arg name "$fs_name" --arg upstream "$upstream_plugins" \
        --slurpfile catalog "$catalog/.manifest.json" '
        ($upstream | split(",") | sort) as $upstream |
        (.objects | keys | sort) as $actual |
        (.source_catalog_hash == $catalog[0].catalog_hash and
         .source_catalog_generation == $catalog[0].generation) and
        (if $name == "threetched" then $actual == $upstream
        else (.objects | has("tched_fs")) and
            ($actual == (($catalog[0].plugins | keys | sort) - $upstream))
        end)
    ' "$mount_path/view.json" >/dev/null
}
if [ -n "$(mounted_kind)" ]; then
    ready || fail 'existing mount differs from the declared identity or release view'
    date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ >"$runtime/fstab-ready-at"
    exit 0
fi
binary=/usr/local/libexec/op-dbus/bin/3tched-fs
store=/dev/shm/3tchedfs-$fs_name
[ -x "$binary" ] && [ -f "$catalog/.manifest.json" ] || fail 'committed release is unavailable'
case "$(findmnt -rn -M /usr/local/libexec/op-dbus/bin -o SOURCE)" in
    opdbus-release:*) ;; *) fail 'application binary target is not an active release' ;;
esac
[ -c /dev/fuse ] || fail 'missing /dev/fuse'
ensure_dir /run/mounts 755
ensure_dir "$mount_path" 755
[ -z "$(find "$mount_path" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -print -quit)" ] || fail 'mountpoint is not empty'
ensure_dir "$store" 700
# Mount sealed declarations before bridge startup. Operations still require
# the existing session and grants; no identity/state is manufactured here.
"$binary" --store "$store" capture --schema-only --catalog "$catalog" --state /dev/shm/opdbus/state \
    "$selection" "$upstream_plugins" >"$runtime/capture.json"
nohup setsid "$binary" --store "$store" mount \
    --fs-name "$fs_name" \
    --catalog /dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs --state /dev/shm/opdbus/state \
    --allow-other --auto-unmount --call-owner-uid "$owner_uid" \
    --lungs-socket /run/opdbus/lungs/lungs.sock --lungs-session "$session" \
    "$mount_path" >"$runtime/daemon.log" 2>&1 </dev/null 9>&- &
daemon_pid=$!
printf '%s\n' "$daemon_pid" >"$runtime/daemon.pid"
attempt=0
while [ "$attempt" -lt 100 ]; do
    if ready; then
        date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ >"$runtime/fstab-ready-at"
        exit 0
    fi
    kill -0 "$daemon_pid" 2>/dev/null || break
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    sleep 0.1
done
kill "$daemon_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
wait "$daemon_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
fail "mount did not become ready; see $runtime/daemon.log"

PATH=/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH
fail() { printf 'mount-3tchedfs: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
case "${1:-}" in
    start)
        [ "$#" = 1 ] || exit 2
        mount /run/mounts/3tchedFS
        exec mount /run/mounts/threetched
        ;;
    stop) exit 0 ;;
esac
[ "$(id -u)" = 0 ] || fail 'host mount owner must be root'
[ "$#" = 4 ] && [ "$3" = -o ] ||
    fail 'expected the declared 3tchedFS fstab entry'
fs_name=$1
mount_path=$2
case "$fs_name:$mount_path" in
    3tchedFS:/run/mounts/3tchedFS) selection=--exclude-plugin ;;
    threetched:/run/mounts/threetched) selection=--include-plugin ;;
    *) fail 'unexpected mount source or target' ;;
esac
upstream_plugins=threetched,tched_router
catalog=/usr/share/op-dbus/plugin-blobs
options=$4
while [ -n "$options" ]; do
    option=${options%%,*}
    case "$option" in
        rw|noauto|nosuid|nodev|noexec|noatime|defaults) ;;
        *) fail "unsupported mount option: $option" ;;
    esac
    case "$options" in *,*) options=${options#*,} ;; *) options= ;; esac
done
protected_file() {
    [ -f "$1" ] && [ ! -L "$1" ] || return 1
    case "$(stat -c '%u:%g:%a' "$1")" in 0:0:400|0:0:600) return 0 ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
}
session_file=/etc/op-dbus/human-lungs-session
owner_file=/etc/op-dbus/human-lungs-call-owner-uid
protected_file "$session_file" && protected_file "$owner_file" || fail 'unsafe or absent host identity selection'
session=$(tr -d '[:space:]' <"$session_file")
printf '%s\n' "$session" | grep -Eq '^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$' || fail 'invalid session'
owner_uid=$(tr -d '[:space:]' <"$owner_file")
case "$owner_uid" in ''|*[!0-9]*) fail 'invalid local caller UID' ;; esac
[ "$owner_uid" = "$(id -u jeremy)" ] || fail 'local operator UID changed'
ensure_dir() {
    if [ ! -e "$1" ] && [ ! -L "$1" ]; then mkdir -m "$2" "$1"; fi
    [ -d "$1" ] && [ ! -L "$1" ] && [ "$(stat -c '%u:%g:%a' "$1")" = "0:0:$2" ] ||
        fail "unsafe directory: $1"
}
ensure_dir /run/opdbus 755
ensure_dir /run/opdbus/host-fuse 700
runtime=/run/opdbus/host-fuse/$fs_name
ensure_dir "$runtime" 700
umask 077
exec 9>"$runtime/adapter.lock"
flock -w 15 9 || fail 'another mount invocation is active'
mounted_kind() { findmnt -rn -M "$mount_path" -o FSTYPE; }
ready() {
    [ "$(mounted_kind)" = fuse.3tchedFS ] || return 1
    [ "$(findmnt -rn -M "$mount_path" -o SOURCE)" = "$fs_name" ] || return 1
    timeout 3 jq -e --arg session "$session" --argjson uid "$owner_uid" '
        .mount_identity.kind == "host_session" and
        .mount_identity.session == $session and
        .local_call_owner_uid == $uid and .workspace_id == null
    ' "$mount_path/.3tchedfs.json" >/dev/null || return 1
    timeout 3 jq -e --arg name "$fs_name" --arg upstream "$upstream_plugins" \
        --slurpfile catalog "$catalog/.manifest.json" '
        ($upstream | split(",") | sort) as $upstream |
        (.objects | keys | sort) as $actual |
        (.source_catalog_hash == $catalog[0].catalog_hash and
         .source_catalog_generation == $catalog[0].generation) and
        (if $name == "threetched" then $actual == $upstream
        else (.objects | has("tched_fs")) and
            ($actual == (($catalog[0].plugins | keys | sort) - $upstream))
        end)
    ' "$mount_path/view.json" >/dev/null
}
if [ -n "$(mounted_kind)" ]; then
    ready || fail 'existing mount differs from the declared identity or release view'
    date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ >"$runtime/fstab-ready-at"
    exit 0
fi
binary=/usr/local/libexec/op-dbus/bin/3tched-fs
store=/dev/shm/3tchedfs-$fs_name
[ -x "$binary" ] && [ -f "$catalog/.manifest.json" ] || fail 'committed release is unavailable'
case "$(findmnt -rn -M /usr/local/libexec/op-dbus/bin -o SOURCE)" in
    opdbus-release:*) ;; *) fail 'application binary target is not an active release' ;;
esac
[ -c /dev/fuse ] || fail 'missing /dev/fuse'
ensure_dir /run/mounts 755
ensure_dir "$mount_path" 755
[ -z "$(find "$mount_path" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -print -quit)" ] || fail 'mountpoint is not empty'
ensure_dir "$store" 700
# Mount sealed declarations before bridge startup. Operations still require
# the existing session and grants; no identity/state is manufactured here.
"$binary" --store "$store" capture --schema-only --catalog "$catalog" --state /dev/shm/opdbus/state \
    "$selection" "$upstream_plugins" >"$runtime/capture.json"
nohup setsid "$binary" --store "$store" mount \
    --fs-name "$fs_name" \
    --catalog /dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs --state /dev/shm/opdbus/state \
    --allow-other --auto-unmount --call-owner-uid "$owner_uid" \
    --lungs-socket /run/opdbus/lungs/lungs.sock --lungs-session "$session" \
    "$mount_path" >"$runtime/daemon.log" 2>&1 </dev/null 9>&- &
daemon_pid=$!
printf '%s\n' "$daemon_pid" >"$runtime/daemon.pid"
attempt=0
while [ "$attempt" -lt 100 ]; do
    if ready; then
        date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ >"$runtime/fstab-ready-at"
        exit 0
    fi
    kill -0 "$daemon_pid" 2>/dev/null || break
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    sleep 0.1
done
kill "$daemon_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
wait "$daemon_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
fail "mount did not become ready; see $runtime/daemon.log"

# 👻 GHOSTBRIDGE LIVE! — Working Wishlist / Task Board

**Ghostbridge Live!** is the name of the whole effort: taking the architecture from
deployed-but-dark to *running live* — registration → Qdrant/Gemma → accountability loop →
routing → chatbot → demo. This board is the single source of truth for all of it.
Replaces scattered TODO fragments across `.zenflow/tasks/`, `.kiro/specs/`, and notebook snapshots.

**Owner topology correction (2026-09-13):** WireGuard terminates at the decoy;
there is no WireGuard on this server. Identity is transported by WARP. Apply
this correction when interpreting older task descriptions. OD-55's source
coverage count does not mean every declared surface requires a server backend;
determine server/decoy applicability or retirement before implementing a handler.

## How to use this board

- **Priority buckets:** Critical/Urgent → Current → Next → Future → When I Have Staff.
- **Status:** `TODO` · `WIP` · `BLOCKED` · `DONE`.
- **Agent:** who's assigned — an `op-agents` role (`devops`, `policy_enforcer`, `schema_as_code`)
  or a Claude Code subagent (`Explore`, `Plan`, `general-purpose`, `claude`).
- **Dispatch:** tell Claude *"dispatch <ID> to <agent>"* — it spawns that agent with the task
  context and updates Status here when done.
- **Add work:** append a row under the right bucket with a fresh `OD-##` id.

# Implementation prompt

Implement threetched consolidation in `/srv/git/odbus-verified`, using the grounded implementation brief included below this prompt in this same file. Read that brief in full before editing.

Read `AGENTS.md` and all its mandatory skill preloads first, then current `HANDOFF.md`, relevant `SIGNALS.md`, `WISHLIST.md`, the brief, and:

- `reports/threetched-overlap-map-20261018.md`
- `reports/threetched-overlap-map-20261018.txt` — JSON method inventory with a sharing-friendly extension.

The original NotebookLM report is a synthesis of supplied sources, not live verification. The grounded brief supersedes its unsupported endpoint names, equivalence claims and automatic test gates. Verify present code and mounted declarations before relying on dated counts or source locations.

## Objective

Collapse handwritten operations already owned by the native threetched runtime into its one native-derived plugin schema. Keep our code under the 3tched distinction and the external ZeroClaw-derived runtime under threetched. Do not relocate duplicate declarations into `large_language_model`, another plugin, a separate schema directory or a new transport shim.

Deliver working implementation and required build/catalog preparation, not another plan. Make the largest coherent, evidence-backed consolidation you can complete without speculative feature expansion. Begin with the direct plugin/skill wrappers, then continue into other established overlaps in dependency order. Explicitly record remaining work and blockers; do not describe a partial slice as complete consolidation.

Full feature parity is not required. Missing persona/configuration features are **OD-122**, and native memory integration is **OD-123**. Those are wishlist work, not prerequisites for unrelated consolidation. Keep **Cozo** as the storage authority. Introduce no SQL/SQLite backend, automatic data migration or silent memory substitution. Existing unrelated migration debt is not this task.

Current access is filesystem I/O, and the current name is **cognitive**. Lungs becomes an MCP interface after consolidation settles; do not implement that future interface here.

## Implementation requirements

1. Claim ownership in HANDOFF before editing. Preserve shared changes. The two direct wrapper modules were already deleted in source, with associated module/dispatch/hash-helper edits, but that removal was not built, sealed or deployed. Reconcile and finish it; do not reset or blindly repeat it.

2. Begin with the mounted namespaces `/run/mounts/threetched` and `/run/mounts/3tchedFS`. Discover supported contracts there. Use pinned native source/export code to diagnose missing capture through the repository's supported maintenance/authoring path. Preserve caller identity and capability checks; do not bypass an absent or denied operation with another identity or transport.

3. Complete the direct-wrapper slice: map all six `tched_plugins` and twelve `tched_skills` operations to the already captured native commands; reconcile arguments/results, callers, exact capabilities, registry/module/dispatch references, generated artifacts and mount selection. The mount adapter currently lists all four upstream IDs. Catalog removal and the adapter must agree.

4. For additional config/provider/cron/router/LLM/cognitive overlap, assign every affected method a concrete disposition: migrate now, retain a genuine local integration responsibility, defer, or retire. Existing caller dependencies identify migration work; they do not justify a second native schema authority. Reconcile callers for removed or deferred behavior and expose truthful unsupported/unavailable outcomes instead of fake success.

5. Add only the native capture required for the selected operations. Extend the existing verified native export/capture and explicit `opblob` authoring boundary. Runtime continues to consume sealed blobs. Do not invent `threetched.Chat`, HTTP endpoints, WebSocket frames or native memory support. The brief contains the observed real names and source references. Missing capture does not mean a feature is absent, and a configuration section is not an HTTP endpoint.

6. Keep identity admission, private state partitions, exact grants, committed SHM publication, receipt/error semantics and cancellation outcomes intact for delivered operations. Do not globally rename state ownership or rewrite grants without tracing the affected contracts. Native stream disconnect does not prove a provider request was undone. No wildcard grants, new identity, blanket capability expansion or security-policy weakening.

7. Update demonstrated consumers across the bridge, generated surfaces, toolsets, the sibling `/srv/git/3tched.com` UI and its pinned release input where affected. A compatibility name may temporarily resolve to the canonical declaration and admission path; it must not establish a separately authored schema. Do not retain wrappers indefinitely merely to avoid migrating callers.

## Build, catalog and deployment boundary

This prompt requests a native GNU release workspace build for the resulting cross-crate change:

```sh
CXXFLAGS="-include cstdint" cargo build --workspace --release --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
```

Use the repository's existing JEV execution routing without model overrides. Run one Cargo process at a time; respect an existing build. Keep the primary agent available for source review and communication. Every delegated agent must perform its own mandatory preload and share task/file ownership.

Use the freshly built `target/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/release/opblob` to prepare a **new isolated catalog** through `seal-plugins <new-catalog-dir>`, with the service's current schema-shaping environment. Review exact added/changed/removed plugin IDs, retain recoverable inputs and ensure matching binaries, generated views, configuration and any affected pinned UI input. Golden consumes the presealed catalog via `OP_PERSISTED_CATALOG_SOURCE`; it does not reseal it.

The default deliverable for this prompt is implemented source, required build results, isolated release inputs and a precise deployment handoff. If the owner separately includes live activation in the receiving task, use only the canonical `./activate-golden.sh` snapshot/send-receive path and its receipts. Never hand-copy application binaries into the live installation. Keep host mount wiring and rollback implications explicit.

Tests, Clippy, formatting checks and custom smoke fixtures run only on explicit owner request. Do not treat the NotebookLM report as permission to run them, and do not make full feature parity or a new test suite a prerequisite for the requested implementation. Use bounded authoring/readiness/operation receipts appropriately and report what was actually checked. Preserve the existing guard/storage hold and deferred subvolume pinning.

## Required handoff

Update HANDOFF, SIGNALS and the existing WISHLIST entries with:

- Current commit and exact changed files, preserving other agents' work.
- Methods/plugins consolidated, retired, retained for a specific local responsibility, or deferred.
- Canonical native targets and important argument/result/capability/state differences resolved.
- Build command and actual result; isolated catalog location, provenance and removal delta.
- Deployment status, unresolved blockers and the exact next action.

Distinguish **proposed, implemented, built, sealed, deployed and tested**. Stop at the authorized delivery boundary. Do not claim complete consolidation, persona equivalence, successful authenticated operation or zero downtime without the corresponding evidence.

# Mastering System Consolidation — grounded implementation brief

**Prepared:** 2026-10-18 by Codex `/root`, task `threetched-single-surface-20261018` / OD-121. **Purpose:** a corrected, actionable version of the NotebookLM synthesis for another LLM to implement. This document is an implementation handoff, not a claim that consolidation has been implemented.

**Owner decisions:** collapse handwritten functionality already owned by threetched into its native schema authority. Useful consolidation does not require full feature parity. Missing persona/configuration and memory integration features are deferred to **OD-122 and OD-123** in [WISHLIST.md](../WISHLIST.md). Keep **Cozo** as the storage authority; introduce no SQL/SQLite backend. Current access is filesystem I/O through `cognitive`; lungs becoming an MCP interface is later work, after consolidation settles.

The original [NotebookLM webpage](<Gemini Notebook - Mastering System Consolidation_ Evidence-Backed Integration of 3tched and threetched.html>) and its supporting assets are preserved. NotebookLM synthesized supplied sources; it did not perform a live audit. This revision grounds its useful proposed sequence in mounted declarations and repository code, and labels remaining assumptions.

## 1. Outcome and implementation scope

The outcome is **one native contract owner for threetched functionality**, projected through our existing filesystem and admission path. A native operation should not have separately authored schemas under `threetched`, `tched_router`, `large_language_model` or another name.

Start with a coherent, useful slice: finish the direct plugin/skill-wrapper consolidation, then migrate additional proven overlaps as their required contracts and callers are understood. Capture only the native contracts needed for the selected slice. Complete the affected source, callers, generated artifacts, mount selections and release catalog together. Do not turn the first slice into a prerequisite to implement every native tool, persona, workflow or memory feature.

For each existing behavior, explicitly select one disposition:

- **Migrate now:** native counterpart established; implement its canonical contract and update callers.
- **Keep as an integration responsibility:** identity admission, scoped context, committed-state publication or receipts still belong to our system. This does not justify independently redefining the native operation.
- **Defer:** record the missing feature and caller impact on the existing task board. Do not expose a fake-success operation or claim parity for deferred behavior.
- **Retire:** remove the declaration and reconcile its callers/policy references; document the resulting feature change.

Removing duplicate declarations is not itself a reason to move or delete authoritative data. Preserve existing principal/session partitions and Cozo data. A compatibility name, if temporarily necessary for a demonstrated caller, must resolve to the one canonical declaration and admission path; it must not become another independently authored plugin schema or permanent wrapper layer.

## 2. Evidence baseline

Evidence labels used below:

- **Mounted:** observed in the identity-bound filesystem declarations during this work.
- **Source:** implementation exists in the inspected checkout or pinned upstream input; this alone does not prove a successful live operation.
- **Proposed:** an implementation choice or sequence, not completed behavior.
- **Deferred/unresolved:** not established or not included in the initial delivery.

| Baseline | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Source HEAD | `051a20d056afba074e21d797aa34f8947c543c5a`, with substantial shared uncommitted work. Do not reset, stash or overwrite it. |
| Our mounted view | `/run/mounts/3tchedFS`: **70 plugins / 1,180 methods**. |
| Upstream mounted view | `/run/mounts/threetched`: **4 plugins / 208 methods**: `threetched` 147, `tched_router` 43, `tched_plugins` 6, `tched_skills` 12. |
| Combined inventory | **74 plugins / 1,388 method declarations**, re-counted from mounted schemas for this revision. |
| Catalog pin | Generation 74, hash `8a34d0da9517b137063314e07f5fa9a24fe3a3fe33920b1de2df941380041fd6`. |
| Native capture | Binary version **threetched 0.8.4**, plugin schema version **1.0.0**, format `threetched-cli/1`, **147 CLI operations / 83 top-level Config sections**. Binary version and plugin schema version are different fields. |
| Native method limits | All 147 CLI methods declare `mutation` and `idempotent=false`; their result envelope is `{stdout, stderr, exit}`. `agent` exists; **`threetched.Chat` does not**. |
| Existing deployment | The earlier deployment receipt records B/root304 as active, release `release-c6ece6d3-7cd5-4761-99a2-56bf684706fe`, with A/root299 previous. This report revision did not activate or independently re-certify the release. |

Primary evidence: [mounted native schema][E1], [mounted catalog view][E2], [full overlap report][E3], [complete method inventory][E4]. The inventory is JSON content saved with a `.txt` extension for sharing; older notes referring to its `.json` filename are stale.

The original map inventories every method; it does not establish end-to-end equivalence for all methods. It explicitly identifies missing native contracts. The NotebookLM sentence saying the map treated CLI help as proof of complete equivalence is removed by this revision.

## 3. What to consolidate

| Surface | Established relationship | Implementation implication |

| `tched_plugins` — 6 | Native `plugin.install/list/migrate/info/remove/search`. | Strong first removal candidate. Confirm arguments, output handling, exact admission and callers against the canonical native operations. |
| `tched_skills` — 12 | Native `skills.add/audit/edit/install/list/remove/test` and `skills.bundle.add/list/remove/rename/show`. | Same first-slice treatment. The 12 native commands are already captured. |
| `large_language_model` — 8 | A facade targeting **tched_router**, not eight already available native CLI replacements. Exact targets below. | Migrate callers to the derived threetched contract when the needed selection/generation operations exist. Moving router declarations into this plugin would preserve duplication. |
| `cron` — 9 | Uses native cron storage. Seven methods relate to CLI actions; history/run use native HTTP routes. | Capture only missing contracts needed for the chosen cron slice. Preserve scope and distinguish accepted backend effects from publication/receipt failure. |
| `mcp` — 3 | `get_config` and `configure_server` delegate to native config through router methods. `configure_tool_groups` is local bridge policy. | Consolidate the two config facades. Assess the remaining policy separately; its name is not an instruction to implement lungs MCP now. |
| `gemma_brain.route` | Delegates to router `ResolveRoute`. | Migrate this operation after native route resolution is mapped. This does not establish equivalence for the other 16 methods. |
| `model_registry.native_list_providers` | Reads native configuration/provider inventory and applies agent-owned-profile/selectability filtering. | Preserve the filtering when migrating. It is not a bare `providers.list` passthrough. |
| Cognitive persona consultations + `specialist` | **568** exposed methods share native provider-only completion. | Shared inference establishes a consolidation opportunity; it does not prove native agent execution reproduces the surrounding context, tools, memory and result behavior. Persona enhancements can be deferred. |

Exact LLM facade targets from [large_language_model_methods.rs][E5]: `list_providers→ListProviders`; `get_provider/get_config→GetState`; `set_provider→SetProvider`; `generate→Chat`; `stream_generate→start_generation`; `list_models→ListModels`; `update_config→SetSelection`. Every target in this sentence currently belongs to **tched_router**. Do not rename it to `threetched.<same-name>` without creating a native-derived contract and implementation.

Other evidence: [cron gateway][E6], [MCP config facade][E7], [provider inventory and filtering][E8], [specialist completion][E9].

### All 43 router methods must have a disposition

Map native configuration/routing separately from local catalog bindings and caller-specific selection. |
| Generation | 7 | `Chat`, `start_generation`, `cancel_generation`, `get_generation_job`, `get_generation_jobs`, `delete_generation_job`, `recover_generation_jobs`. Native inference exists. Local jobs, revisions, publication, cancellation and recovery have separate implementation obligations. |

Evidence: [mounted router schema][E10], [router declaration source][E11], [generation job dispatcher][E12]. No requirement is imposed to reproduce every router feature in the first release. Every removed or deferred feature must nevertheless have an explicit disposition and reconciled callers.

### Coverage of the rest of the catalog

The complete 74-plugin disposition table and method names remain in [the overlap map][E3] and [machine inventory][E4]. Its classification totals are:

| Classification | Plugins | Methods | Meaning |
|---|---:|---:|---|

| Wrapper | 3 | 26 | Confirmed delegation; not automatically identical typed contracts. |
| Mixed | 6 | 748 | Shared native behavior plus local obligations or capture gaps. |
| Candidate | 12 | 73 | Functional overlap requiring a narrower comparison or deliberate deferral. |
| Different scope | 35 | 236 | Current evidence distinguishes the responsibilities. This is not a permanent exemption from future consolidation. |
| Unestablished | 17 | 158 | No equivalent established by this capture. It does not mean the plugin is broken or native threetched cannot implement the feature. |
| **Total** | **74** | **1,388** | Audit categories, not runtime routing rules. |

Candidates include `agent_config`, `persona`, `memory`, `embedding_model`, `workflows`, `project` and related application behavior. The NotebookLM blanket statement that all of `project` is proven unique and must remain is too strong: memberships/ACLs/documents and native workspace/context behavior need separate dispositions. Likewise, config sections named `storage`, `backup`, `tunnel` or `security_ops` do not prove equivalence to our Btrfs, database or host-administration operations.

In the prior map, notation such as `/agents`, `/memory`, `/shell_tool` and `/project_intel` denotes **configuration sections**, unless explicitly identified as an HTTP route. Do not invent endpoints from those names.

## 4. Native capture and the schema-to-blob boundary

The present implementation is:

1. Explicit `opblob` sealing calls `threetched::prepare_schema_capture`.
2. The selected binary/manifest are checked; the capture reads native `config schema`, recursive command `--help`, version and binary digest.
3. `schema_from_capture` derives the threetched PluginSchema. Separately registered handwritten plugins still produce their own PluginSchemas.
4. `opblob` seals each full PluginSchema into the blob catalog. Full reseal removes plugin IDs absent from the build.
5. Golden preparation stages the already sealed catalog; snapshot send/receive and activation transport it. FUSE projects the resulting declarations and committed state.

Evidence: [explicit sealer][E13], [capture owner][E14], [CLI capture implementation][E15], [full-schema blob serialization][E16]. Duplicate authoring enters **before sealing**; a shared catalog alone does not remove it.

### Capture gaps and concrete evidence

| Area | Grounded evidence | Work needed for a selected implementation slice |
|---|---|---|
| Native HTTP config | Pinned gateway `openapi.rs::build_spec` derives schemas from native Rust types; gateway declares `/api/openapi.json`. `api_config.rs` defines property/list/patch/init/migrate types and errors. | Import the relevant native-owned contract with provenance. Do not assume the current CLI capture already includes HTTP results/errors. |
| OpenAPI coverage | The inspected source includes config/version paths, `/api/skills/slash-option-kinds`, additional schema components, and a feature-gated A2A addition. It is not an export of every gateway or WebSocket operation. | Inventory actual exported coverage. Earlier shorthand “config/version only” was incomplete; neither that shorthand nor the generated lesson is sufficient authority for coverage. |
| Native tools | Current adapter reads `/api/tools`: name, description, parameters and optional output. Its local type deliberately omits native `param_domains`. | Preserve needed native metadata when deriving the chosen methods. Agent/config-dependent tool visibility must not turn a capture identity's tools into universal grants. |
| Cron | Source declares `/api/cron`, `/api/cron/{id}`, `/api/cron/{id}/runs` and `/api/cron/{id}/run`. | Use these verified paths. The lesson's `/cron/history` and `/cron/run` are not the inspected routes. |
| Provider-only generation | Pinned patch exposes `/ws/chat?stateless_generation=1`, protocol `tched_router.generation.v1`, strict connect/message inputs and session_start/connected/chunk/done/error outputs. | Export/derive the native frame contract for the generation slice. No existing `threetched.Chat` method should be assumed. |
| Cancellation and receipts | Native stateless code drops the provider stream on disconnect and notes that the remote provider may already have accepted input. Local `cancel_generation` checks job revision, commits state and signals a worker. | Preserve truthful cancellation/state outcomes. These are source observations, not live endpoint calls.

**Proposed implementation rule:** extend the existing explicit authoring/capture boundary and, where necessary, the pinned native export. Derive selected operations from native types/exports; retain binary, patch, version and schema provenance. Runtime consumers continue to use the sealed catalog. Do not add another repository `schemas/` authority, live schema fallback, generic parallel API client or second control plane. Unsupported capture remains an explicit gap or deferred feature.

Do not require complete HTTP/tool/WebSocket capture before removing the already captured plugin/skill wrappers. Capture becomes necessary when a selected migration depends on the missing contract.

## 5. Cognitive: complete counts and a bounded proposal

| Group | Methods | Current evidence / disposition |
|---|---:|---|
| Persona consultations | 567 | 81 personas × seven verbs. Shared native inference; persona/config improvements deferred under OD-122. |
| Execution catalog | 59 | 12 aliases backed by five executors. Existing dispatch uses identity-bearing `UnifiedExecution` D-Bus calls. Native shell/runtime overlap is a candidate, not proven language-operation equivalence. |
| Orchestration catalog | 18 | Six agents × three operations. Each child goes through canonical admission with the original caller. Native SOP/pipeline comparison may be deferred. |
| Memory operations | 7 | `memory_store/retrieve/query/recall/delete/list_namespaces/semantic_query`. Existing scoped Cozo owner, optional Qdrant semantics. OD-123 covers future native integration. |
| Code retrieval/indexing | 3 | `code_search`, `code_context`, `code_index`: Voyage/Qdrant and session-aware context. Generic native project/memory sections do not establish equivalent retrieval. |
| Compatibility agent facades | 6 | `rust_pro`, `python_pro`, `typescript_pro`, `sequential_thinking`, `context_manager`, `code_review_orchestrator`. |
| Workflow facades | 2 | `workflow_query/run`, sharing the local workstack owner. |
| Specialist/provider calls | 2 | `specialist` plus `gemini_query`; the latter has separate provider/research behavior. |
| Discovery/admission/policy | 6 | `get_health`, `list_tools`, `invoke_tool`, `schema_read`, `oscal_subids`, `toolsets`. |
| **Total** | **670** | **644 agent methods + 26 other methods.** |

The lesson's abbreviated list totaled 660. Persona consultations alone are **84.6%** of 670, not “over 85%.” These are generated declarations from [agent descriptors][E20], not 567 independently handwritten function implementations. The opportunity is reducing duplicate exposed contracts and local behavior that native facilities can own.

### What a persona migration actually needs to map

[specialist.rs][E9] shows that current consultations do more than append a static role: they validate the persona/verb, resolve the caller's route and mode, select a memory namespace, assemble dynamic persona pieces and scoped context, add role/knowledge, preserve the operation in the prompt, recheck admission, invoke provider-only completion and construct typed persona/source metadata.

The mounted Config's `AliasedAgentConfig` supports `identity`, `knowledge_bundles`, `skill_bundles`, `model_provider`, `risk_profile`, `runtime_profile`, `workspace`, `memory` and related fields. It has **no direct `system_prompt` field**. `IdentityConfig` supports OpenClaw/AIEOS documents and AIEOS inline/file sources. These establish native configuration mechanisms, not a completed translation of our prompt assembly.

**OD-122 proposal:** move static role/knowledge into appropriate native identity/bundle facilities where useful; map verbs, dynamic context and result metadata separately. Do not make exact reproduction of all 567 legacy method names a prerequisite for the first consolidation slice. Do not silently change provider-only consultation into tool-enabled agent execution.

**OD-123 proposal:** retain Cozo ownership and scope. The mounted `AgentMemoryConfig.backend` defaults to `sqlite`; `MemoryBackendKind` declares none/sqlite/postgres/qdrant/markdown/lucid, with no Cozo option. That is a concrete future integration gap. It is not authorization to add SQL/SQLite, switch stores, migrate data or silently disable memory. Other consolidation can proceed while this work stays on the wishlist.

Evidence: [mounted Config inside the native schema][E1], [specialist context/completion][E9], [execution dispatch][E21], [workflow admission][E22]. No agent configuration or memory backend was changed while preparing this brief.

## 6. Dependencies the implementing LLM must reconcile

| Dependency | Required treatment |
|---|---|
| Callers | Trace exact plugin/method references through bridge dispatch, UI, schema loaders, toolsets and generated outputs. Inspect the sibling UI's `src/chat/{door-chat-adapter,native-routing,control-plane-model,router-committed-route}.ts` and `src/grpc/door.ts`; do not assume one file handles every caller. Update the pinned UI input when the changed UI is part of a release. |
| Schema ownership | Make native operation shapes derive from the one native contract. Local policy/receipt integration must not independently reauthor native arguments/results. Never invent the target method name because the old owner used it. |
| State | Identify existing public/private state and child objects before changing owner paths. Preserve principal/session scope, unrelated children and authoritative Cozo data. Commit actual backend results to canonical SHM before notifications. Do not assume a global rename to `threetched` preserves state isolation. |
| Capability mapping | Build explicit old-method → canonical-operation → exact-capability mappings. Read/write distinctions, actor/session admission and current grants must survive. A hashed CLI capability is not automatically equivalent to an old typed read capability. No wildcard grants or direct policy rewrites to hide denials. |
| Receipts/errors | Distinguish execution failure, backend acceptance, state-publication failure, cancellation and recovery. A successful filesystem write or CLI exit alone is not proof of the full operation. |
| Mount selection | The host adapter currently hardcodes `threetched,tched_router,tched_plugins,tched_skills`. Update it consistently with actual catalog removals. Preserve our/upstream naming and separation. [Adapter source][E23]. |
| Generated/release inputs | Remove obsolete module/registry/dispatch references, regenerate affected derived views through existing mechanisms, prepare an isolated catalog, review exact added/changed/removed plugin IDs and stage the matching binaries/config/UI. Do not hand-edit generated output as a second authority. |

For capability changes, preserving existing authorization is not permission to broaden it. Follow the repository's smallest-concrete-change procedure if a genuinely new grant is required. An operation denial is evidence to diagnose, not a reason to switch identities or transports.

## 7. Implementation sequence and completion evidence

This is a proposed sequence for the receiving agent. The owner asked this author to produce a prompt/document, not execute the application changes.

1. **Reconcile the shared work first.** Read current AGENTS/HANDOFF/SIGNALS and the mounted catalog. Two direct wrapper modules were already deleted in source before the mapping hold, with related edits in `mod.rs`, `threetched.rs` and `mutation_engine.rs`; those removals remain unbuilt/unsealed/undeployed. Preserve unrelated work and finish this slice coherently rather than restarting it.
2. **Finish the directly captured wrapper slice.** Resolve plugin/skill command inputs, outputs, capabilities and callers against the 18 native commands. Reconcile mount selections and generated inputs. Record any feature deliberately retired/deferred instead of introducing replacement duplicate schemas.
3. **Migrate further proven overlaps in dependency order.** Select the next useful config/provider/cron/router subset. Add only the native capture needed by that subset; retain required local admission/state/receipt integration. Do not hold the first slice for full persona, memory or workflow parity.
4. **Build and prepare the release inputs.** Follow JEV's Cargo routing, one Cargo process, native `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, release `CXXFLAGS="-include cstdint"`. Use the freshly built `opblob` for an isolated `seal-plugins <new-catalog-dir>` catalog with matching schema-shaping environment. Review removals and preserve recovery inputs. Golden consumes the already sealed catalog via `OP_PERSISTED_CATALOG_SOURCE`; it does not reseal it.
5. **Hand off with exact status.** Report changed files, implemented/retired/deferred methods, build result, catalog delta, remaining blockers and next action. Live deployment, when explicitly included in the receiving task, uses `./activate-golden.sh` and snapshot send/receive; never hand-copy application binaries into the running host. Track host mount wiring separately from the application snapshot.

Evidence for a completed implementation slice includes resolved callers, one schema owner, exact catalog delta, successful required build and consistent release inputs. If deployed, add native activation/readiness receipts, mount/catalog agreement and resulting authoritative state where an admitted operation is available. Missing identity provisioning or an unavailable operation remains an explicit limitation.

**Tests, Clippy, formatting checks and custom smoke fixtures remain owner-request-only.** The NotebookLM `cargo check --workspace` and persona-test gates are not automatic authority to run checks. Workspace scope and build execution follow the receiving prompt and current AGENTS. Report unrun tests as unrun. There is no claim of zero risk, guaranteed zero downtime or complete semantic parity.

Existing guard/storage holds and later subvolume pinning remain outside this scope. Future lungs MCP is neither a dependency of the first consolidation slice nor an interface to implement now.

## 8. What is ready to hand off

- **Grounded baseline:** mounted counts, real method names, native Config fields, current source ownership and the actual cron/generation/tool contract evidence.
- **First implementation slice:** finish the existing plugin/skill-wrapper removal and reconcile callers, mount selection, generated inputs and release catalog.
- **Subsequent slices:** migrate proven native overlap as needed contracts become available; track selected behavior and dependencies explicitly.
- **Deferred enhancements:** OD-122 native persona/configuration mapping; OD-123 Cozo-backed native memory integration. These do not block unrelated consolidation.
- **Current authoring status:** documentation and task-board changes only; no new application implementation, build, seal, deployment, grants, mounts or storage changes.

The implementation prompt is at the top of this file. The receiving LLM must reread present sources and shared ownership; this evidence is dated, not a substitute for current state.

# Agent Patterns

Multi-agent design, delegation, and orchestration in Claude Code and AI-assisted development. Default to fungible agents for large-scale software dev; use specialized agents only for peer review or discourse-based workflows.

Subagents in Claude Code are specialized AI assistants that run in isolated context windows with custom system prompts, specific tool access, and independent permissions. They preserve main conversation context by keeping exploration, test runs, and verbose operations out of the primary thread.

Key constraint: subagents cannot spawn other subagents. Multi-step orchestration requires chaining subagents from the main conversation.

## Quick Reference

| Pattern                   | Description                                       | When to Use                                  |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| Fungible swarm            | Identical agents pick tasks from a shared board   | Large-scale software dev, resilient systems  |
| Sequential pipeline       | Each agent builds on previous output              | Multi-step workflows with clear dependencies |
| Hierarchical              | Manager decomposes, workers execute in parallel   | Complex tasks with independent subtasks      |
| Peer collaboration        | Agents iterate until consensus                    | Code review, quality-critical outputs        |
| Orchestrator delegation   | Main conversation chains subagents                | Multi-phase workflows, parallel specialists  |
| Two-stage review          | Spec compliance check, then code quality check    | High-stakes code, complex requirements       |
| Question-first delegation | Agent asks clarifying questions before proceeding | Ambiguous tasks, expensive-to-redo work      |
| Review loop enforcement   | Fix-review cycle with max iteration escalation    | Any review workflow needing convergence      |

| Built-in Subagent | Model    | Tools     | Purpose                                           |
| ----------------- | -------- | --------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| Explore           | Haiku    | Read-only | File discovery, code search, codebase exploration |
| Plan              | Inherits | Read-only | Codebase research during plan mode                |
| General-purpose   | Inherits | All tools | Complex research, multi-step operations           |
| Bash              | Inherits | Terminal  | Running terminal commands in separate context     |
| Claude Code Guide | Haiku    | Read-only | Answering questions about Claude Code features    |

| Configuration            | Value                                                                             |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Custom agent location    | `.claude/agents/*.md` (project), `~/.claude/agents/*.md` (user)                   |
| CLI agents               | `--agents '{...}'` (session only, JSON format)                                    |
| Plugin agents            | Plugin `agents/` directory (lowest priority)                                      |
| Required fields          | `name`, `description`                                                             |
| Optional fields          | `tools`, `disallowedTools`, `model`, `permissionMode`, `skills`, `hooks`, `color` |
| Model values             | `sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku`, `inherit` (default)                                    |
| Permission modes         | `default`, `acceptEdits`, `dontAsk`, `bypassPermissions`, `plan`                  |
| Nesting limit            | Subagents cannot spawn other subagents (one level only)                           |
| Foreground vs background | Foreground blocks main conversation; background runs concurrently                 |
| Batch size               | 5-8 items per agent (standard tasks)                                              |
| Parallel agents          | 2-4 simultaneously                                                                |

## When to Use Subagents vs Main Conversation

| Use Subagents When                                              | Use Main Conversation When                                 |
| --------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| Task produces verbose output (test suites, logs, API responses) | Task needs frequent back-and-forth or iterative refinement |
| Enforcing specific tool restrictions or permissions             | Multiple phases share significant context                  |
| Work is self-contained and can return a summary                 | Making a quick, targeted change                            |
| Parallel independent research paths                             | Latency matters (subagents start fresh and gather context) |

## Tool Access Patterns

| Agent Role         | Recommended Tools                       | Rationale                                     |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| Read-only reviewer | `Read, Grep, Glob`                      | Cannot modify code; safe for audits           |
| File creator       | `Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep`         | NO Bash; avoids heredoc approval spam         |
| Script runner      | `Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep, Bash`   | Full access for build/deploy tasks            |
| Research agent     | `Read, Grep, Glob, WebFetch, WebSearch` | External data access for documentation lookup |

Subagents inherit all tools by default (including MCP tools). Use `tools` as an allowlist or `disallowedTools` as a denylist to restrict access. MCP tools are not available in background subagents.

## Common Mistakes

| Mistake                                                     | Correct Pattern                                                                                            |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Expecting subagents to spawn sub-subagents                  | Subagents cannot nest; chain subagents from the main conversation instead                                  |
| Giving Bash tool to agents that only create files           | Use Write and Edit tools only; Bash causes approval spam from heredoc usage                                |
| Omitting `disallowedTools` for sensitive operations         | Use `disallowedTools` to explicitly deny dangerous tools even when inheriting                              |
| Spawning too many agents (5+) for a small task              | Start with 2-3 agents; coordination overhead outweighs benefit at higher counts                            |
| Burying critical instructions past line 300 of agent prompt | Put critical rules immediately after frontmatter; models deprioritize late instructions                    |
| Using specialized agents for large-scale software dev       | Use fungible agents with a shared task board; specialized agents create single points of failure           |
| Not including "FIX issues found" in delegation prompts      | Without explicit action directive, agents only report problems without making changes                      |
| Setting model to Haiku for content generation               | Default to Sonnet; Haiku only for script execution, fast lookups, or pass/fail checks                      |
| Not writing clear descriptions for custom agents            | Claude uses the `description` field to decide when to auto-delegate; vague descriptions prevent delegation |
| Using MCP tools in background subagents                     | MCP tools are not available in background subagents; run in foreground instead                             |
| Not preloading skills into subagents                        | Subagents do not inherit skills from the parent; list them explicitly in the `skills` field                |

## Delegation

- **Explore codebase before designing agent prompts**: Claude auto-delegates to the built-in Explore subagent (Haiku, read-only) for file discovery and code search; supports quick, medium, and very thorough modes
- **Plan multi-agent architecture for complex projects**: Use plan mode; Claude delegates research to the Plan subagent before presenting a plan
- **Execute batch operations across many files**: Chain General-purpose subagents from the main conversation with identical prompts and non-overlapping item lists
- **Isolate high-volume operations**: Delegate test runs, log processing, or doc fetching to subagents to keep verbose output out of your main context
- **Run parallel research**: Spawn multiple subagents simultaneously for independent investigations; Claude synthesizes findings when all complete
- **Resume interrupted work**: Ask Claude to continue a previous subagent; resumed agents retain full conversation history including tool calls and reasoning

> For project-level workflow sequencing, phase-gate validation, goal decomposition, and capability scoring, use the `orchestration` skill.

## References

- [Agent types and design patterns](references/agent-types.md)
- [Delegation patterns and batch workflows](references/delegation-patterns.md)
- [Sub-agent configuration and prompt engineering](references/sub-agent-configuration.md)
- [Communication and orchestration patterns](references/orchestration.md)
- [Troubleshooting and anti-patterns](references/troubleshooting.md)

# Shared 3tched resources

cognitive-mcp links to the existing cognitive MCP plugin, including the declared
agent_* operations. agent-config links to the existing agent configuration owner.
Use their current schemas and admitted operations. These links do not create a
second agent registry, start agents, or grant tools.

threetched-plugins links to the tched_plugins owner for installed extension
packages. Its methods map the threetched binary's plugin commands. Installation
and runtime selection are separate: the existing tched_router configuration
owner controls plugins.enabled, plugins.plugins_dir and signature policy.
Agent skill selection uses agents.<alias>.skill_bundles and the referenced
skill_bundles.<alias>.include/exclude settings through that same owner.

Discover current operations through this identity's mounted 3tchedFS namespace
at /run/mount/3tchedfs. Verify supported paths and method schemas there rather
than assuming a copied catalog matches the running service.

Keep shared resources free of personal records, private conversations and secrets.
Changes to an accepted shared base require a new base and deliberate migration.

# Verification Before Completion

## Overview

**Core principle:** Evidence before claims, always.

**Violating the letter of this rule is violating the spirit of this rule.**

## The Iron Law

```
NO COMPLETION CLAIMS WITHOUT FRESH VERIFICATION EVIDENCE
```

If you haven't run the verification command in this message, you cannot claim it passes.

## The Gate Function

```
BEFORE claiming any status or expressing satisfaction:

1. IDENTIFY: What command proves this claim?
2. RUN: Execute the FULL command (fresh, complete)
3. READ: Full output, check exit code, count failures
4. VERIFY: Does output confirm the claim?
   - If NO: State actual status with evidence
   - If YES: State claim WITH evidence
5. ONLY THEN: Make the claim

Skip any step = lying, not verifying
```

## Common Failures

| Claim | Requires | Not Sufficient |
|-------|----------|----------------|
| Tests pass | Test command output: 0 failures | Previous run, "should pass" |
| Linter clean | Linter output: 0 errors | Partial check, extrapolation |

| "Agent said success" | Verify independently |
| "I'm tired" | Exhaustion ≠ excuse |
| "Partial check is enough" | Partial proves nothing |
| "Different words so rule doesn't apply" | Spirit over letter |

```
❌ "Tests pass, phase complete"
```

**Agent delegation:**

```
❌ Trust agent report
```

**ALWAYS before:**
- ANY variation of success/completion claims

## Overview

**Core principle:** Evidence before claims, always.

**Violating the letter of this rule is violating the spirit of this rule.**

## The Iron Law

```
NO COMPLETION CLAIMS WITHOUT FRESH VERIFICATION EVIDENCE
```

If you haven't run the verification command in this message, you cannot claim it passes.

## The Gate Function

```
BEFORE claiming any status or expressing satisfaction:

1. IDENTIFY: What command proves this claim?
2. RUN: Execute the FULL command (fresh, complete)
3. READ: Full output, check exit code, count failures
4. VERIFY: Does output confirm the claim?

5. ONLY THEN: Make the claim
```

deployed-but-dark to *running live* — registration → Qdrant/Gemma → accountability loop →
routing → chatbot → demo. This board is the single source of truth for all of it.

determine server/decoy applicability or retirement before implementing a handler.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Populate an unaccepted, externally prepared base. Caller owns storage resealing.
set -euo pipefail
fail() { printf 'ERROR: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
[[ $# == 2 && $(id -u) == 0 ]] || fail 'usage (root): populate.sh BASE_TOPLEVEL PREPARED_ASSETS'
base=$(realpath -e -- "$1")
assets=$(realpath -e -- "$2")
[[ $base != / && -f $base/@/etc/os-release ]] || fail 'invalid base'
[[ $(findmnt -rn -M "$base" -o FSTYPE) == btrfs && $(findmnt -rn -M "$base" -o FSROOT) == / ]] || fail 'requires mounted Btrfs top level'
[[ $(findmnt -rn -M "$base" -o OPTIONS) == *rw,* ]] || fail 'caller must prepare writable base'
for member in memory rules shared skills soul user; do
    target=$base/@agent_$member
    [[ -d $target && ! -L $target ]] || fail "missing sibling: $member"
    btrfs subvolume show "$target" >/dev/null
    [[ -z $(find "$target" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -print -quit) ]] || fail "refusing nonempty sibling: $member"
    [[ -d $assets/$member && ! -L $assets/$member ]] || fail "missing assets: $member"
    [[ -z $(find "$assets/$member" -type l -print -quit) ]] || fail 'asset symlinks must be authored explicitly'
    [[ -d $base/@/agent/$member && ! -L $base/@/agent/$member ]] || fail 'unsafe guest mountpoint'
    [[ -z $(find "$base/@/agent/$member" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -print -quit) ]] || fail 'guest mountpoint must remain empty'
done
for entry in AGENTS.md SOUL.md USER.md MEMORY.md; do
    [[ ! -e $base/@/agent/$entry && ! -L $base/@/agent/$entry ]] || fail "existing guest entry: $entry"
done
[[ ! -L $base/@/etc/3tched ]] || fail 'unsafe host-folder mountpoint'
if [[ -e $base/@/etc/3tched ]]; then
    [[ -d $base/@/etc/3tched && -z $(find "$base/@/etc/3tched" -mindepth 1 -print -quit) ]] || fail 'host-folder mountpoint must be empty'
fi
for member in memory rules shared skills soul user; do
    cp -a "$assets/$member/." "$base/@agent_$member/"
    chown -R root:root "$base/@agent_$member"
    find "$base/@agent_$member" -type d -exec chmod 0755 {} +
    find "$base/@agent_$member" -type f -exec chmod 0644 {} +
    diff -qr "$assets/$member" "$base/@agent_$member"
done
chmod 0700 "$base/@agent_memory" "$base/@agent_rules" "$base/@agent_user"
chmod 0700 "$base/@agent_rules/rules" "$base/@agent_user/user"
chmod 0600 "$base/@agent_rules/rules/rules.md" "$base/@agent_user/user/user.md"
install -d -m 0700 "$base/@agent_user/identity"
for method in memory_store memory_recall memory_retrieve memory_query memory_delete memory_list_namespaces memory_semantic_query; do
    ln -s "/run/mount/3tchedfs/plugins/cognitive/operations/$method" "$base/@agent_memory/$method"
done
ln -s rules/AGENTS.md "$base/@/agent/AGENTS.md"
ln -s soul/SOUL.md "$base/@/agent/SOUL.md"
ln -s user/USER.md "$base/@/agent/USER.md"
ln -s memory/MEMORY.md "$base/@/agent/MEMORY.md"
ln -s /run/mount/3tchedfs/plugins/cognitive "$base/@agent_shared/cognitive"
ln -s /run/mount/3tchedfs/plugins/agent_config "$base/@agent_shared/agent-config"
ln -s /run/mount/3tchedfs/plugins/tched_plugins "$base/@agent_shared/threetched-plugins"
ln -s /run/mount/3tchedfs/plugins/tched_router "$base/@agent_skills/runtime"
ln -s /run/mount/3tchedfs/plugins/tched_skills "$base/@agent_skills/skills"
install -d -m 0755 "$base/@/etc/3tched"
for member in skills rules user shared soul memory; do
    ln -s "/etc/3tched/$member" "$base/@agent_$member/host"
done
manifest=$base/@/usr/share/op-dbus/agents/workspace
install -d -m 0755 "$manifest"
(
    cd "$base"
    find @agent_memory @agent_rules @agent_shared @agent_skills @agent_soul @agent_user -type f -print0 |
        sort -z | xargs -0 sha256sum
) > "$manifest/SHA256SUMS"
printf '%s\n' 'Shared templates only. No identity database or private data initialized. Runtime loading requires explicit integration.' > "$manifest/README"
sync -f "$base"
printf 'Populated six agent siblings; kept guest mountpoints empty and authored workspace links.\n'

#!/bin/sh
# op-dbus-release: application
# The controller publishes these shipped bytes to the canonical SHM catalog.
# SchemaLoader (server.rs GetSchema) caches them until bridge restart/reload.
# op-dbus-consumes: /usr/share/op-dbus/plugin-blobs
exec 2>&1

startup_phase() {
    printf 'op-grpc-bridge startup phase=%s pid=%s\n' "$1" "$$"
}
startup_phase identity-selector

# Explicit root-owned initialization selector; absent during normal boot.
identity_init=/etc/op-dbus/initialize-local-human
unset OP_LOCAL_HUMAN_INITIALIZE_SESSION
if [ -e "$identity_init" ] || [ -L "$identity_init" ]; then
    [ ! -L "$identity_init" ] && [ -f "$identity_init" ] &&
        [ "$(stat -c %u:%g:%a "$identity_init")" = 0:0:600 ] &&
        [ "$(stat -c %s "$identity_init")" -le 37 ] || exit 1
    OP_LOCAL_HUMAN_INITIALIZE_SESSION=$(cat "$identity_init")
    export OP_LOCAL_HUMAN_INITIALIZE_SESSION
fi

# Operator-assigned NextDNS context for this exact WireGuard identity. This is
# sealed by MutationEngine, never supplied by the browser or inferred from DNS.
# An explicit [] enables legacy-only minting for a compatibility rollout.
if [ "${OP_IDENTITY_NEXTDNS_BINDINGS+x}" != x ]; then
    OP_IDENTITY_NEXTDNS_BINDINGS='[{"wireguard_pubkey":"0I5FNCuHAu62VctaNgOlJ7RgfejJpYe9Qd0VdPGesX8=","profile_id":"689ec7","device_name":"Ghostbridge-Incus"}]'
fi
export OP_IDENTITY_NEXTDNS_BINDINGS

DEFAULT_READY_PATH=/run/opdbus/runit-ready/op-grpc-bridge
rm -f -- "$DEFAULT_READY_PATH"

wait_dep() {
    startup_phase "dependency:$1"
    sv start "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    i=0
    until sv check "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1; do
        i=$((i+1))
        [ "$i" -ge 90 ] && { echo "dependency $1 not ready after 90s" >&2; exit 1; }
        sleep 1
    done
    startup_phase "dependency-ready:$1"
}

# Nothing in the boot path calls back into this service: ovs-vswitchd
# materializes the topology from conf.db and the ovsbr0-* units use plain `ip`.
# That absence of a back-edge is what keeps this list cycle-free — check it with
# deploy/runit/check-dep-cycles.py before any reboot.
wait_dep opdbus-rundirs
wait_dep opdbus-grants
wait_dep dbus
wait_dep unified-execution
wait_dep op-runit-systemctl
wait_dep op-session-bus
wait_dep identity-roots
wait_dep ovsdb-server
wait_dep tched-router
# Identity storage restoration is owned independently by identity-roots. The
# bridge waits for the storage owner's readiness before restoring active
# service identities. The storage owner never depends on this bridge.
# Qdrant is optional here. The bridge initializes its semantic shuttle
# best-effort and must still open :8090 for D-Bus and gRPC when vector search
# is unavailable.

startup_phase configuration
set -a
[ -r /etc/op-dbus/environment ] && . /etc/op-dbus/environment
[ -r /etc/op-dbus/decoy-network-client.env ] && . /etc/op-dbus/decoy-network-client.env
set +a

# A dedicated directory can be mounted through Incus without exposing the
# bridge's other runtime sockets. The bridge authenticates host callers or
# derives guest identity from kernel peer credentials and native Incus state.
export OPDBUS_LUNGS_SOCKET=/run/opdbus/lungs/lungs.sock

# The native router's provider-only generation protocol requires a real paired
# subject. Consume the operator-provisioned token from a root-only file; never
# accept the secret itself from the broad environment file.
export TCHED_ROUTER_RUNTIME_ENDPOINT="${TCHED_ROUTER_RUNTIME_ENDPOINT:-http://127.0.0.1:8084}"
export TCHED_ROUTER_RUNTIME_AGENT="${TCHED_ROUTER_RUNTIME_AGENT:-dashboard}"
# Door selection is not limited to OpenCode profiles.
export TCHED_ROUTER_REQUIRE_OPENCODE=0
startup_phase runtime-token
TCHED_ROUTER_RUNTIME_TOKEN_FILE=${TCHED_ROUTER_RUNTIME_TOKEN_FILE:-/etc/op-dbus/secrets/tched-router-runtime-token}
unset TCHED_ROUTER_RUNTIME_TOKEN
if [ ! -f "$TCHED_ROUTER_RUNTIME_TOKEN_FILE" ] || [ -L "$TCHED_ROUTER_RUNTIME_TOKEN_FILE" ]; then
    echo "protected tched_router runtime token file is missing or not a regular file" >&2
    exit 78
fi
set -- $(stat -Lc '%u %a' "$TCHED_ROUTER_RUNTIME_TOKEN_FILE")
[ "$1" -eq 0 ] && { [ "$2" = 400 ] || [ "$2" = 600 ]; } || {
    echo "tched_router runtime token file must be root-owned with mode 0400 or 0600" >&2
    exit 78
}
TCHED_ROUTER_RUNTIME_TOKEN=$(cat "$TCHED_ROUTER_RUNTIME_TOKEN_FILE")
case "$TCHED_ROUTER_RUNTIME_TOKEN" in
    ''|*[!A-Za-z0-9._~-]*)
        echo "tched_router runtime token file has an invalid token" >&2
        exit 78
        ;;
esac

## The Rule

**Invoke relevant or requested skills BEFORE any response or action** — including clarifying questions, exploring the codebase, or checking files. If it turns out wrong for the situation, you don't have to use it.

**Before entering plan mode:** if you haven't already brainstormed, invoke the brainstorming skill first.

## Skill Priority

When multiple skills apply, process skills come first — they set the approach, then implementation skills (frontend-design, etc.) carry it out. Brainstorming and systematic-debugging are Superpowers' most common process skills, but the rule holds for any of them.

- "Let's build X" → superpowers:brainstorming first, then implementation skills.
- "Fix this bug" → superpowers:systematic-debugging first, then domain skills.

These thoughts mean STOP—you're rationalizing:

| Thought | Reality |
|---------|---------|
| "This is just a simple question" | Questions are tasks. Check for skills. |
| "I need more context first" | Skill check comes BEFORE clarifying questions. |
| "Let me explore the codebase first" | Skills tell you HOW to explore. Check first. |

| "The skill is overkill" | Simple things become complex. Use it. |

| "This feels productive" | Undisciplined action wastes time. Skills prevent this. |
| "I know what that means" | Knowing the concept ≠ using the skill. Invoke it. |

---

<SUBAGENT-STOP>
If you were dispatched as a subagent to execute a specific task, ignore this skill.
</SUBAGENT-STOP>

<EXTREMELY-IMPORTANT>
If you think there is even a 1% chance a skill might apply to what you are doing, you ABSOLUTELY MUST invoke the skill.

IF A SKILL APPLIES TO YOUR TASK, YOU DO NOT HAVE A CHOICE. YOU MUST USE IT.

This is not negotiable. You cannot rationalize your way out of this.
</EXTREMELY-IMPORTANT>

## The Rule

**Invoke relevant or requested skills BEFORE any response or action** — including clarifying questions, exploring the codebase, or checking files. If it turns out wrong for the situation, you don't have to use it.

**Before entering plan mode:** if you haven't already brainstormed, invoke the brainstorming skill first.

Then announce "Using [skill] to [purpose]" and follow the skill exactly. If it has a checklist, create a todo per item.

## Skill Priority

When multiple skills apply, process skills come first — they set the approach, then implementation skills (frontend-design, etc.) carry it out. Brainstorming and systematic-debugging are Superpowers' most common process skills, but the rule holds for any of them.

- "Let's build X" → superpowers:brainstorming first, then implementation skills.
- "Fix this bug" → superpowers:systematic-debugging first, then domain skills.

## Red Flags

These thoughts mean STOP—you're rationalizing:

| Thought | Reality |
|---------|---------|
| "This is just a simple question" | Questions are tasks. Check for skills. |
| "I need more context first" | Skill check comes BEFORE clarifying questions. |
| "Let me explore the codebase first" | Skills tell you HOW to explore. Check first. |
| "I can check git/files quickly" | Files lack conversation context. Check for skills. |
| "Let me gather information first" | Skills tell you HOW to gather information. |
| "This doesn't need a formal skill" | If a skill exists, use it. |
| "I remember this skill" | Skills evolve. Read current version. |
| "This doesn't count as a task" | Action = task. Check for skills. |
| "The skill is overkill" | Simple things become complex. Use it. |
| "I'll just do this one thing first" | Check BEFORE doing anything. |
| "This feels productive" | Undisciplined action wastes time. Skills prevent this. |
| "I know what that means" | Knowing the concept ≠ using the skill. Invoke it. |

## Platform Adaptation

If your harness appears here, read its reference file for special instructions:

- Claude Code: `references/claude-code-tools.md`
- Codex: `references/codex-tools.md`
- Pi: `references/pi-tools.md`
- Antigravity: `references/antigravity-tools.md`
- Hermes Agent: `references/hermes-tools.md`
- Muse: `references/muse-tools.md`

## User Instructions

User instructions (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md, etc, direct requests) take precedence over skills, which in turn override default behavior. Only skip skill workflows or instructions when your human partner has explicitly told you to.

28:                            plugin_methods.proto from every plugin's schema.methods,

31:                         b) DYNAMIC: crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/dynamic_reflection.rs
32:                            (ActiveReflectionCatalog) hydrates live from the sealed
33:                            SHM blob catalog via hydrate_reflection_from_shm() —
34:                            this is the "frozen" descriptor set for what's actually
35:                            present right now, independent of what's compiled in.
36:5. Frozen            → the blob + its descriptors are immutable once sealed.
37:6. gRPC socket = hot → crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/grpc_server.rs registers the
38:                       generated per-plugin service (plugin_method_routes.rs,
39:                       add_routes()) on the tonic UDS bridge, dispatching each
40:                       RPC to call_generated_plugin_method_typed(plugin_id,
41:                       schema_name, ...) which routes through PluginService.CallMethod
